chapter.name: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds

questions.stem: Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen fails for which of the following compounds?
questions.solution: Lassaigne's test for nitrogen requires both nitrogen and carbon to be present in the organic compound to form $\mathrm{CN^-}$ ions upon fusion with sodium metal. Hydrazine ($\mathrm{H_2N-NH_2}$) does not contain carbon, so it cannot form $\mathrm{NaCN}$ and thus fails Lassaigne's test.

questions.stem: In Dumas method for estimation of nitrogen, $0.3	ext{ g}$ of an organic compound gave $50	ext{ mL}$ of nitrogen collected at $300	ext{ K}$ and $715	ext{ mm}$ pressure. If the aqueous tension at $300	ext{ K}$ is $15	ext{ mm}$, the percentage of nitrogen in the compound is ________. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Pressure of dry $N_2$ gas: $P = 715 - 15 = 700\text{ mm Hg}$
Using $PV = nRT \Rightarrow n = \frac{PV}{RT} = \frac{(700/760) \times 0.050}{0.0821 \times 300} \approx 0.001869\text{ mol}$
Mass of $N_2 = 0.001869 \times 28 = 0.05233\text{ g}$
\% of nitrogen = $\frac{0.05233}{0.3} \times 100 \approx 17.44\% \approx 17\%$.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen, the blue colour is due to the formation of:
questions.solution: During Lassaigne's test, sodium fusion extract containing $\mathrm{NaCN}$ is reacted with $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ and acidified with $\mathrm{HCl}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ions, forming Prussian blue, which is ferriferrocyanide, $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$.

questions.stem: In the Kjeldahl's method for estimation of nitrogen in an organic compound, $0.28	ext{ g}$ of the compound was digested and the ammonia evolved was absorbed in $20	ext{ mL}$ of $0.1	ext{ M}$ sulphuric acid. The excess acid required $20	ext{ mL}$ of $0.1	ext{ M}$ sodium hydroxide for complete neutralization. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is ______ %.
questions.solution:
Initial milliequivalents of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 20 \times 0.1 \times 2 = 4\text{ meq}$.
Milliequivalents of $\text{NaOH} = 20 \times 0.1 \times 1 = 2\text{ meq}$.
Milliequivalents of acid reacted with $\text{NH}_3 = 4 - 2 = 2\text{ meq} = 2\text{ mmol}$ of nitrogen.
Mass of nitrogen $= 2 \times 10^{-3} \times 14 = 0.028\text{ g}$.
Percentage of nitrogen $= \frac{0.028}{0.28} \times 100 = 10\%$.
